We identified cluster markers using the wilcoxauc function implemented by the presto package and defined significant cluster markers with Wilcoxon rank-sum test Benjamini–Hochberg-adjusted P < 0.05, expressed cell percentage difference (pct_in) > 10%, expression logFC > 0.1.

TRM cell-type annotation was performed on the cluster level. We first annotated epithelial cells (EPCAM+), B cells (CD79B+) and proliferative CD4+ T cells (MKI67+), then annotated non-proliferative T cell subtypes based on mapping to a public adult human intestine tissue immune cell reference with two complementary approaches. We identified cell-type markers of the in vitro and tissue data separately using the wilcoxauc function with cut-off Wilcoxon rank-sum test Benjamini–Hochberg-adjusted P < 0.05, expressed cell percentage difference > 10%, expression logFC > 0.1. We quantified the marker gene overlap significance between in vitro and tissue cell types using −log10-transformed Fisher’s two-sided exact test nominal P value. For each in vitro cell type, we got the top three tissue cell types with the strongest overlap, or the subset of top three if the significance difference between pairs of top three was larger than 10. In parallel, we calculated Spearman correlation between our in vitro and tissue cell types based on the markers defined in both systems. For each in vitro cell type, we got the top three tissue cell types showing the highest transcription program similarity, or the subset of top three if the significance difference between pairs of top three was larger than 0.1. We then annotated the in vitro T cells as the overlap of overlap-based and similarity-based matched tissue cell types. On the basis of further inspection of individual canonical marker gene expression, we manually renamed activated CD4 T, activated CD8 T and MAIT-like CD4 as CD4 TRM, CD8 TRM and CD4 TRMTH17, respectively.

In a recent development, to construct an adult human intestine tissue transcriptome reference, we collected the count matrix and cell-type annotation of epithelial cells from three public adult intestine multi-region scRNA-seq datasets79,80,81. All datasets were processed using Seurat (v4). After merging the datasets, we performed LogNormalize normalization with a scale factor of 10,000. We identified HVGs independently for each dataset using the vst method, selecting 3,000 HVGs per dataset. We then selected integration features across datasets using the SelectIntegrationFeatures function. We ran principal component analysis using the selected integration features and retrieved the top 50 principal components. We integrated the data with Cluster Similarity Spectrum (CSS)82 stratified by sample, and default setting for other parameters. We performed dimension reduction with UMAP, and Louvain clustering based on CSS embeddings using the FindNeighbors and FindClusters functions at a resolution of 1.0. We compared the data without batch effect correction, integration with Harmony or with CSS integration, and chose CSS-integrated results based on visual inspection of canonical cell-type marker gene expression.

To establish a consistent cell-type annotation scheme across datasets, we created a mapping between original annotations and standardized categories. We classified cells into major epithelial lineages: absorptive cells (enterocytes and colonocytes), goblet cells, BEST4+ cells, EECs, follicle-associated epithelium, stem cells, M cells, Paneth cells, secretory progenitors and tuft cells. We further refined these annotations by incorporating regional information. We defined the G2M-phased cells defined by the CellCycleScoring function in Seurat within the clusters with enriched expression of MKI67 as the transit-amplifying cells. Cell-type identities were validated using established marker genes. For rare cell populations (for example, Paneth cells and tuft cells), we calculated expression-based scores using canonical markers (DEFA5 and DEFA6 for Paneth cells; RGS13, AVIL and ALOX5 for tuft cells) and assigned cells based on these scores. To be more specific, we identified the top five positively correlated genes with summarized DEFA5 and DEFA6 scaled expression profiles across epithelium among the 3,000 HVGs as feature genes of Paneth cells. We summed up the scaled expression levels of the selected top five Paneth-associated genes for each cell as the Paneth cell feature score, and defined cells with scores exceeding 97.5th percentile of all positive scores as Paneth cells. We applied a similar procedure to identify tuft cells, with 10 tuft cell feature genes and using 95 percentile as the selection cut-off.

To establish a tissue reference for colonocyte subtype annotation in the Salmonella dataset, we subsetted to non-small intestine transit-amplifying cells, stem cells and colonocytes, integrated the data with CSS and performed subclustering based on the CSS embeddings at resolution = 0.4. We identified cluster markers using the wilcoxauc function in the presto package, with cut-offs adjusted P < 0.05, pct_in > 10 and logFC > 0.1. We selected the top 100 markers ranked by logFC from each cluster and unified them as features for comparison between in vitro and tissue colonic stem cells and colonocytes.

Recent findings suggest that to further reconstruct the differentiation trajectory from stem cells to colonocytes in primary tissues (excluding transit-amplifying cells), we computed a diffusion map using the DiffusionMap function in the destiny package on the CSS space and we defined the rank of the first diffusion component (DC1) as the inferred differentiation pseudotime. We ordered the cells along the pseudotime, partitioned them into 25 bins and calculated the average gene expression of each bin. We calculated the Pearson correlation coefficients between the bin average expression levels and the bin order for each gene. The 50 genes with the strongest positive correlations were selected as pseudotime-positive correlating genes, which show higher expression levels in mature colonocytes, and the 50 genes with the strongest negative correlations as pseudotime-negative correlating genes, which show higher expression levels in stem cells and early colonocytes. We then applied these tissue-derived differentiation-related genes on the sorted infection dataset. We used the AddModuleScore function in Seurat based on normalized RNA expression values of the pseudotime positively and negatively correlating genes separately. A composite differentiation score of the cells in the chip was defined as the difference between the positive and negative module scores. We ordered the colonocytes according to the differentiation score from premature to mature, partitioned them into 25 bins and calculated the average gene expression of each bin. The obtained bin average gene expression profiles are defined as expression profiles along the reconstructed pre-mature-to-mature colonocyte differentiation trajectory.

To create a unified peak list across samples, we called open chromatin-accessible regions in each sample using MACS2 (v2.2.9.1) with the CallPeaks function and then quantified them with FeatureMatrix in Signac. We only kept regions located on standard chromosomes. We annotated peaks to most nearby genes using the annotatePeak function in ChIPseeker based on the Ensemble (v98) annotation. We only retained cells with ATAC UMI count between 200 and 50,000, RNA UMI count less than 20,000, RNA gene number between 500 and 5,000, mitochondrial percentage less than 50%, nucleosome signal (calculated by NucleosomeSignal) less than 1, transcription start site enrichment score (calculated by TSSEnrichment) less than 1 and hg38 genome blacklist ratio less than 0.5%. We ran the same pipeline of scRNA-seq data from read count normalization to dimension reduction and clustering as described in the previous section (‘Preprocessing and cell-type annotation of scRNA-seq data’). For the scATAC-seq data, we performed term frequency-inverse document frequency normalization on read counts using the RunTFIDF function. We defined the regions with over 1% detection rate as top features and RunSVD based on the top features. We projected cells into two-dimension UMAP embeddings and FindNeighbors based on top 2–50 latent semantic indexing.

Sources indicate that we performed major epithelial cell-type annotation on RNA cluster level based on canonical cell-type marker expression. We subsetted to colonic stem cell and colonocyte clusters, calculated the Spearman correlation coefficients between in vitro and tissue stem cell to colonocyte clusters using the in vitro-expressed colonic stem cell and colonocyte feature genes defined in the tissue reference. We performed hierarchical clustering on the in vitro clusters based on the similarity profiles and classified them into stem cells and four colonocyte subtypes indicating differential maturity accordingly. Colonocyte clusters with mostly exclusive presence in the Salmonella-infected sample were defined as infection-specific colonocyte clusters. We transferred RNA-level cell-type annotations to ATAC data, and merged subtypes that could not be clearly resolved by ATAC data as annotations on the ATAC level.

Industry observers note that we performed differential analysis for co-clustered S.Tm infection and control cells in each cluster of stem cells, colonocytes and goblet cells, which have sufficient cell numbers for robust estimation. For infection-specific clusters, which have less than 20 control cells in the clusters, we first identified matched control sample cells for each infected sample cell using get.knnx of the FNN package with k = 1 in the top 20 principal component space. We identified DEGs between matched control and infected cells using the wilcoxauc function by the presto package, with cut-offs adjusted P < 0.05, pct_in > 10 and logFC > 0.1. We applied the same procedure to identify DEGs in the epithelium induced by TRM cell co-culture except that we did not need to use the k-nearest neighbour search approach to get matched control cells as there was no condition-specific cluster.

Industry observers note that to identify DARs between Salmonella-infected and control conditions, we implemented a statistical framework based on linear regression modelling of binarized chromatin accessibility data, with sequencing depth (UMI counts) as covariate. Specifically, for each open chromatin region i, we fitted:.

Null model: glm(e ~ UMIcounts, family = binomial).

Full model: glm(e ~ UMIcounts + condition, family = binomial).

Industry observers note that where e represents the binarized accessibility state vector for region i across all cells. We applied a Chi-squared test comparing the two models using ANOVA. Regions were considered differentially accessible if they had Benjamini–Hochberg-adjusted P < 0.05 and showed at least a 0.5% difference in the proportion of cells with the region accessible between Salmonella-infected and control conditions.

We reconstructed the gene regulatory networks from the scMultiome data along the stem-cell-to-coloncyte trajectory and each of the stem cell, colonocyte and goblet cell types shared by both control and infection conditions using Pando83 separately. We used the infection-induced DEGs and 5,000 HVGs of each data as input HVGs for Pando. We constrained our candidate regulatory regions to be either conserved in mammals (defined in phastConsElements20Mammals.UCSC.hg38 provided by Pando) or overlapped with ENCODE regions (defined in SCREEN.ccRE.UCSC.hg38 provided by Pando), and showing significantly correlated profiles with HVGs as output by LinkPeaks in Signac at the default distance threshold of 500 kb. We ran find_motifs and used the Pando-provided transcription factor-binding site (TFBS) motif database compiled from JASPAR and CIS-BP as reference for Pando to identify TFBS in candidate regulatory regions. We ran the infer_grn function with a Gaussian generalized linear model (model = ‘glm’) to infer regulatory coefficients from log-normalized transcript counts and binarized peak counts summarized to SLM algorithm-defined ATAC clusters (resolution = 10). We identified transcription factor–target gene modules using the find_modules function with default settings. We combined the modules from different datasets as inferred transcription factor–target pairs.

For visualization, we selected the condition-dependent DEGs with the top 500 absolute value of expression log-transformed fold change between conditions and the union set of the top three-correlated Pando-predicted transcription factors of each selected DEGs. We calculated pairwise Pearson correlation coefficients of expression profiles across cell types and conditions between selected genes, reduced the dimension of obtained correlation matrix to 20 principal components using prcomp_irlba in the irlba package and further projected genes to two-dimension embeddings using umap in the uwot package with the obtained principal components as input.

It has been revealed that we ran the AddMotifs function in Signac to add the TFBS motifs information on our detected open chromatin regions and obtained a motif occurrence matrix. To identify TFBS motifs over-represented in open chromatin regions with increased accessibility upon infection in each cell type, we ran FindMotifs in Signac on the top 200 upregulated accessible regions, with 30,000 open chromatin regions with matched overall GC content retrieved by the MatchRegionStats function as background.

In a recent development, we defined three comparisons to characterize the luminal effects: (1) ΔSPI-1/2 non-invaded (ΔSPI-1/2Out, GFP−) versus non-infected, (2) WT non-invaded (WTOut, GFP−) versus non-infected, and (3) WTOut versus ΔSPI-1/2Out; and three for intracellular effects: (1) WT invaded (WTIn, GFP+) versus WTOut, (2) ΔsteE invaded (ΔsteEIn, GFP+) versus WTIn, and (3) ΔSPI-2In versus WTIn. We subsetted to colonocytes. Genes detected in at least 50 colonocytes were retained, excluding features with Ensembl-style identifiers beginning with ‘ENSG’. Pairwise comparisons were conducted between predefined experimental conditions within each colonocyte cluster. Comparisons were performed only when at least 20 cells were available in at least one condition. When one of the conditions contained fewer than 20 cells, we supplemented with cells from other clusters of the same condition that were defined as nearest neighbours of the other condition, using get.knnx of the FNN package with k = 1 based on Euclidean distance in the top 20 principal component space. Differential expression testing was performed using the wilcoxauc function of the presto R package on normalized RNA expression values. We identified DEGs between conditions per cluster using the wilcoxauc function by the presto package, with cut-offs adjusted P < 0.05, pct_in > 10 and logFC > 0.1.

We then pooled genes defined as significant DEGs in at least one comparison in at least one cluster as the union set of condition DEGs. We then calculated the colonocyte average expression levels of each condition. We calculated the expression difference between WTOut and non-infected—namely, diff_WT_vs_NI, where positive values indicate upregulation in WTOut versus non-infected—and between WTIn and WTOut—namely, diff_WT_GFP_vs_WT, where positive values indicate upregulation in WTIn versus WTOut. We ranked the gene according to diff_WT_vs_NI, took the top 50 genes as feature genes and used the AddModuleScore function to calculate the luminal effect gene module score, and applied the same procedure for diff_WT_GFP_vs_WT values for intracellular effect gene module score.

Industry observers note that we used CellChat (v2)84 to infer intracellular communications between co-cultured intestinal epithelial cells and TRM cells. Normalized expression data were extracted from the epithelium and TRM cell combined Seurat RNA assay, and cell-type labels were used to group cells for interaction analysis. We used the built-in human CellChatDB database as reference for ligand–receptor interactions. To reduce computational cost, we subsetted the expression data to include only signalling genes present in the database. Overexpressed genes and interactions were identified using the identifyOverExpressedGenes and identifyOverExpressedInteractions functions. Communication probabilities were computed using the computeCommunProb function with type = truncatedMean and trim = 0.05. We subsetted to interactions between proximal small intestinal enterocytes and immune cell types, excluding proliferating CD4+ T cells for visualization.

Read alignment, gene expression quantification and cell filtering of the VASA-seq data were performed by Single Cell Discoveries. In brief, raw sequencing data were processed using Cutadapt (v4.9) to remove adapter sequences and homopolymers, followed by Ribodetector (v0.3.1) to filter out ribosomal reads. Processed reads were then aligned to the reference genome using STARsolo (v2.7.11b), with the parameter–soloFeatures set to GeneFull_Ex50pAS. The human reference genome used was GRCh38, ENSEMBL release 103. The S.Tm reference genome was downloaded from EnsemblBacteria Salmonella enterica subsp. enterica serovar Typhimurium str. 14028S str. LT2 14028S (GCA_000022165) release 62. The resulting single-cell-level gene count matrices were used as inputs for downstream analysis in R.

To improve the gene annotation for the S.Tm genome, we performed sequence alignment for the genes in the S.Tm strain 14028S annotation against the S.Tm strain 14028 annotation (GCF_028596185.1_ASM2859618v1). Out of the 1,542 genes with Ensembl-style identifiers beginning with ENSB, 242 were mapped to annotated genes with common names in the S.Tm 14028 annotation by blastn85,86 with more than 90% of sequence similarity.

Recent findings suggest that cells without GFP signal, UMI count of less than 3,500 or External RNA Controls Consortium (ERCC) counts of less than 450 were excluded. Raw counts were normalized using the NormalizeData function in Seurat with a scale factor of 10,000.

Industry observers note that according to FACS index sorting values, cells with GFP < 500 were defined as GFP−, 500 or more and less than 2,000 as GFPlo, 2,000 or more and 10,000 or less as GFPint, and more than 10,000 as GFPhi. For human genes, only genes detected in at least 10% of cells in at least one GFP signal group were included in the differentially expressed test. For each retained gene, expression was modelled using two nested linear models. The reduced model included log-transformed total UMI counts per cell and the percentage of mitochondrial reads as technical covariates, whereas the full model additionally included the GFP signal group as a factor. The contribution of the GFP signal group was assessed by ANOVA comparing the full and reduced models. Genes with Benjamini–Hochberg-adjusted P < 0.05 were considered differentially expressed. To assign directionality, we calculated the difference in average expression between the GFPhi and GFPlo groups and assigned the directionality accordingly.

For S.Tm, we applied the same differentially expressed test strategy, but only included GFP+ cells for comparison. Given the sparsity of the bacteria transcripts, we reduced the detection rate cut-off to 1%. After further excluding ERCC transcripts and features with Ensembl-style identifiers beginning with ENSB, 3,137 genes were left as input for the differentially expressed test. We used nominal P < 0.05 as the cut-off to get marginally significant bacterial DEG.

Fragment files of scMultiome are available at Mendeley Data (https://doi.org/10.17632/8pt6w6fc7m). The raw flow cytometry data files used to generate the immune UMAP have been deposited in the Zenodo repository87 (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21786694). Source data underlying all graphical representations used in the figures are provided as Supplementary Information. Public adult intestine multi-region scRNA-seq datasets were retrieved from an interactive website of the Space-Time Gut Cell Atlas (https://www.gutcellatlas.org/)79, ArrayExpress (E-MTAB-10187)81 and Gene Expression Omnibus (GSE185224)80.

The core scripts of single-cell data analysis are available on GitHub (https://github.com/devsystemslab/Host-microbe_interaction_model/).

According to recent reports, R.L.-S., M.F.H., Q.Y., M.N., N.G. and J.G.C. conceived the study. R.L.-S., M.F.H., Q.Y., N.G. and J.G.C. wrote the manuscript. M.N. designed and fabricated the fluidic device and crypt stamps, with support from J.A. and S.M. M.P.L. contributed to the development of the fluidic device holding the tissues. M.N. and R.L.-S. generated the artwork design. M.F.H. and R.L.-S. designed and performed most of the experiments in the article. R.L.-S., M.F.H., M.N., N.A. and J.B. optimized the epithelium growth conditions. M.F.H. isolated the organoid lines and TRM cells from primary tissue. R.L.-S., M.F.H., M.A.-B., L.G.-T. and S.S. performed scRNA-seq, scMultiome and VASA-seq experiments. M.A.-B. and L.G.-T. generated the sequencing libraries. Q.Y. performed the computational analysis of scRNA-seq and scMultiome data, with support and data interpretation from R.L.-S., S.S. and M.F.H. M.F.H., R.L.-S. and J.A. co-developed the histomold. I.C. and S.T. performed the FFPE processing, sectioning, H&E and AlcianBlue–PAS stainings, with support from M.F.H. M.F.H. performed the immunohistochemistry and mIF stainings, imaging and analysis with support from R.L.-S. and M.N. M.F.H., R.L.-S., M.N. and L.K. performed whole-mount stainings and imaging. M.F.H., K.K. and S.K. performed the flow cytometry experiments and analysis of immune cells. R.L.-S., D.C. and I.C.-A. performed the flow cytometry and image stream experiments and analysis of epithelial cells. L.K., A.M.F. and M.F.H. performed the cytokine measurements. N.A., S.R.V., Y.B. and J.B. generated the organoid reporter lines. J.F., A.A. and C.S. performed and processed the proteomic measurements. Live imaging was performed by M.F.H., R.L.-S. and M.N., and analysed by M.B. M.H. and D.B. generated and provided the S.Tm strains. T.R. and F.G. supported with data interpretation. All authors read and approved the manuscript.

a) Picture of a chip-slide with culture medium, including a 3D-rendered image of the cross-section of the chip-slide containing three individual chip segments and an image of the micropatterned stamp with a representative bright-field image of an engineered intestine cross-section, e > 15. b) Time course of biomimetic epithelium formation from the stamped empty ECM to epithelium coverage and maturation. Scale bars: 500 µm. c) Quantification of viable crypts of 16 donors from duodenum, ileum and colon, d = 16. d) Representative EDF brightfield image of a Z-stack, showing the top-view of a day-9 epithelium, e = 3. Scale bar: 200 µm. The magnified insert (top) shows a 3D-reconstruction of the epithelium with crypts penetrating into the matrix. The magnified insert (bottom) shows an EDF image of a Z-stack in the crypt area. Scale bar: 50 µm. e) Representative EDF fluorescent image of selected Z-stacks with magnified insert, showing an iCas9 CDH1-mScarlet3 day-9 duodenal epithelium with tight E-Cadherin+ adherens junctions (red), e = 6. Scale bar: 100 µm. f) Overview of the high-throughput histo-processing workflow using 3D-printed histomold facilitating co-planar embedding of up to fifty engineered epithelia at once. Post-FFPE embedding, dozens of engineered epithelia can be visualized within one section as illustrated in a representative H&E. Consecutive sections subjected to H&E and mIF to evaluate the spatial organization and maturation of a duodenal epithelium at day 6. Scale bar: 100 µm. g) H&E cross-sections of representative colon engineered epithelium and primary tissue, showing high morphological similarity, crypt depth, and goblet cell distribution, e = 5. Scale bars: 100 µm.

a-c) Representative mIF cross-section of engineered duodenal, ileal and colonic epithelia in direct comparison to the donor-matched primary tissue (ileum not matched), highlighting the stem-niche specific SOX9+ (cyan) and transit-amplifying Ki67+ cells (pink), matching abundance of MUC2+ goblet cells (green) and high expression of the region-enriched absorptive lineage marker (orange) in the E-Cadherin+ epithelium (grey). The duodenal epithelium was marked by strong expression APOA4+ enterocytes, matching the parental tissue. Expression of distal FABP6+ enterocytes in the top-layer of the engineered epithelium matched ileal tissue. The colonic epithelium exhibited CA1+ colonocytes at comparable levels to the organ of origin, e = 4. Scale bars: 50 µm.

a) Representative H&E images of engineered duodenal epithelia over 10 days of maturation, highlighting epithelial polarization, thickening, and increasing crypt depth, e = 3. Scale bar: 50 µm. b) Representative mIF images of spatiotemporal patterning of SOX9+ (cyan) and Ki67+ (red) cells of E-Cadherin+ (orange) duodenal epithelium over 10 days, e = 3. Scale bar: 100 µm. c) Representative mIF showcasing crypt and top layer annotations and cell segmentation with respective masks for SOX9+ (cyan) and Ki67+ cells (red), e = 3. 💡 Key Takeaways

  • Seeking their first-ever away victory in the MLS Cup playoffs, Charlotte FC will visit SeatGeek Stadium on Sunday for game one of their best-of-three series with the Chicago Fire.
  • The Fire finished fourth in the Eastern Conference this year, losing their last outing 4-3 to the Columbus Crew as they wound up a point above Charlotte, who drew 3-3 with Inter Miami on Decision Day.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Joel Lefevre | 19 Nov 2026 23:33.

Seeking their first-ever away victory in the MLS Cup playoffs, Charlotte FC will visit SeatGeek Stadium on Sunday for game one of their best-of-three series with the Chicago Fire.

The Fire finished fourth in the Eastern Conference this year, losing their last outing 4-3 to the Columbus Crew as they wound up a point above Charlotte, who drew 3-3 with Inter Miami on Decision Day.

Throughout 2026, Chicago were out to prove that last year was no fluke as they continued to improve in the league yet again.

In his second year as head coach, Gregg Berhalter saw his team gain two more points than in his inaugural campaign, while finishing four places higher in the Eastern Conference table this time around and making the playoffs on successive occasions.

The next step will be for the Fire to find some playoff success, with this club aiming to advance beyond the first round for the first time since 2009.

During this regular season campaign, they won three more home matches when compared to 2025, though they have only won one playoff fixture in Illinois since 2009, defeating Orlando City 3-1 in the Wildcard Round a year ago.

They have points in three of their last four MLS encounters but will try to snap a two-match domestic losing run at home this weekend, conceding a combined seven goals in those two defeats.

On Sunday, the Fire can beat Charlotte at home for a third consecutive occasion, having won those last two contests by a single goal.

The Crown are back in the post-season for a third successive occasion, hoping to get past round one at long last.

Dean Smith’s men set a single-season club record for goals scored in 2026 (66), averaging just under two per match (1.9) in the league this year.

This weekend, they will hope to end a four-match domestic winless run away from home and collect their first-ever road triumph in the post-season.

Defensively, they have been shaky as the visitors in 2026, conceding three or more goals on eight occasions in the regular season.

In round one of the playoffs, they have netted just one goal overall and have never scored in the opening half of an MLS road playoff game.

Charlotte have also never won a post-season game in normal time, and have scored first only once, in 2024 when they lost to Orlando City on penalties in the decisive third game of that best-of-three opening round series.

Chicago Fire Major League Soccer form:.

Charlotte FC Major League Soccer form:.

Due to a knock, Inter Miami loanee Noah Allen is questionable for the Fire, as is Robin Lod, who has a leg injury.

Robert Lewandowski has three goals in his last two games, netting a brace in their defeat to the Crew, with Maren Haile-Selassie also scoring on Decision Day.

On the Charlotte side, Tim Ream is questionable as he recovers from an adductor issue, Archie Goodwin may not be available due to a foot problem, Nimfasha Berchimas is recovering from foot surgery and Aron John is dealing with a shoulder injury.

Liel Abada notched a pair of goals in their regular-season finale, while a 90th-minute strike from Rodolfo Aloko earned them a point against the reigning MLS Cup champions.

Chicago Fire possible starting lineup:.

Brady; Dean, Hanche-Olsen, Elliott, Gutman; Saletros, D’Avilla, Haile-Selassie; Zinckernagel, Lewandowski, Bamba.

Charlotte FC possible starting lineup:.

Kahlina; Byrne, Agyemang, Kessler, Toffolo; Diani, Westwood, Biel; De La Torre, Toklomati, Saint-Maximin.

Massive players elevate their games in big moments, and Lewandowski has usually been a difference-maker at club level, we believe his consistency and lethal finishing will prove decisive on Sunday.

Sheffield United have reportedly shown interest in re-signing defender Rob Holding.

The 31-year-old is best-known for his exploits in the colours of Arsenal, who he represented between 2016 and 2023 after cutting his teeth at Bolton Wanderers.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Holding later moved to Crystal Palace, who loaned the centre-back to Sheffield United for the second half of the 2024/25 season.

He helped the Blades reach the Championship play-off final, making 11 appearances before seeing his Palace contract come to an end.

There was talk of a return to Bramall Lane but a reunion did not materialise and Holding went stateside to sign for Colorado Rapids.

He is not under contract for the 2027 Major League Soccer season and according to Sky Sports, Sheffield United have shown interest.

Holding is also noted to have caught the eye of Los Angeles FC and Houston Dynamo, who appear to have been impressed by his MLS showings.

Sheffield United manager Chris Wilder is already familiar with Holding and he would add a wealth of experience to the Blades ranks.

However, the prospect of remaining in the MLS - and living in LA or Houston - could prove tempting.

When Sheffield United recruited Holding in 2025, Wilder described him as “the last remaining piece of the jigsaw”.

He remarked: “It is the last remaining piece of the jigsaw and whilst we have had to wait until deadline day to get this one boxed off, I think our patience has been justified by getting Rob over the line.

“He's played in some huge games during his time with Arsenal, so he'll relish the situation he's walking into. He'll compete with the likes of Anel [Ahmedhodzic], Jack [Robinson] and others, and joins a squad which is looking far healthier than the one we had at the start of the window, as we look to attack the remaining part of the season.”.

Published: 06:21 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 14:24 EST, 16 November 2026.

Lamine Yamal mercilessly taunted England rival Elliot Anderson as tensions flared during the Three Lions’ spectacular victory over Spain on Sunday night.

England held on for a memorable 3-2 victory in Madrid after Anderson was given his marching orders with just under 30 minutes remaining.

Thomas Tuchel’s side were three goals in front and cruising when Anderson - looking to atone for a sloppy error from Jarrel Quansah - cynically hauled down 19-year-old Yamal as he barrelled down on goal.

Spain were awarded a penalty for the infringement, and Anderson was sent off - much to the Manchester City star’s bemusement.

According to recent reports, but Yamal, aggrieved by Anderson’s challenge, made a beeline for the midfielder following the challenge. According to Spanish reports, the attacker mouthed ‘tonto, tonto’ to his rival following his dismissal.

The colloquial term can mean a number of things, varying from idiot, fool or stupid, but in any case is far from a term of affection.

🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨بطاقة حمراء لإليوت أندرسون ولامين يامال يستفزه🤯🤯#اسبانيا_انجلترا #دوري_الأمم_الأوروبية pic.twitter.com/cOrswp5kCC.

Lamine Yamal was spotted taunting Elliot Anderson after the Manchester City midfielder was sent off for a challenge on the winger.

The moment came in England's historic 3-2 win over the World Champions.

Anderson blanked the 19-year-old while a VAR review confirmed the on-field official’s decision was the right one, eventually trudging off the pitch.

A fired-up Yamal galvanised the reigning world champions as they searched for an unlikely comeback.

Mikel Oyarzabal, the man who scored Spain’s winner against England two years ago in the 2024 Euros final, converted the spot kick before Nico Williams scored Spain’s second after latching on to an excellent Yamal cross.

However, Las Rojas fell short, with Sunday’s defeat their first in an imperious 43-game run.

A jubilant Thomas Tuchel hailed the match as his ‘best performance of my time as manager’.

According to recent reports, ‘What a performance we put out there for 60 minutes to be deservedly 3-0 up,’ Tuchel remarked after the game. ’Thirty minutes against Spain with ten men feels like three hours.

‘It was a statement victory. It was on the highest level football-wise. It is a wonderful feeling for us in the dressing room.’.

Wilder, whose side welcome Watford this weekend, mentioned: "He's had an operation. He's going to be out for 12 months. Straight away, I think we all knew where that was going, how awkward he landed. And straight away, I think you always go on the reaction of the players.

In a recent development, "It's a long recovery for him and a testing time for him and a testing time for us because we're losing an attack-minded player that we're looking forward to getting back amongst us. He was finding his feet, he was coming off the bench and he most probably would have been in contention to start now. But that's not the case.

"He's devastated, as we all are. We're devastated for him because this is a substantial injury for him. One hundred per cent, it will make a full recovery.

Blaster had his ACL and there's other injuries that we've had and we've had to get over, as everybody else and other clubs will have to do. But it's a real big blow, it's a hammer blow for us and even more so for the boy, especially at his age and when he's starting to kick on.".

Meanwhile, Wilder insists he remains relaxed regarding recent speculation regarding key midfielder Sydie Peck, rumoured to be on the wanted list of Premier League clubs in the January window.

North-east duo Newcastle United and Sunderland have been linked with moves, but Wilder is obviously keen to retain the player - while being pragmatic that things could change if a huge massive-money offer was tabled.

Wilder, who has Patrick Bamford back available, said: "We talked about extending the contracts of the young players and Sydie's one of those players that we'd love to have that discussion with.

"(But) If anything comes up that you can't turn down, I don't think anybody would turn that down. I've noted it all along, you're not just turning that from a club's point of view, you're turning that down from an opportunity for the player to go and play in the Premier League. I'm glad (about) that because that weren't happening about 15 months ago, the value of the players was zero.

"The previous year, the value of the players, in my opinion, was about £100 million and that's what happens when you win games of football and you get a team together and you build a team that wins.

Sources indicate that "We're trying to reset that and rebuild those values of the players and all players have got a value. When the young players are playing well - they're not babies no more, but they're still relatively young in their careers and have Championship experience - then we're happy because they're playing consistently well.

"When that happens, if that happens, and I'm sure it will happen, then we'll deal with that. My sole focus, which I've mentioned and I've used this word over the last three or four months, is building a group, not just off the back of one pre-season.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Sam Varley | 19 Nov 2026 23:37.

Aiming to break into the top eight of the Championship table on their return from the November international break, Sheffield United will welcome Watford to Bramall Lane on Saturday.

The hosts lost in their final game before the break but sit just two points outside of the playoff spots, while their visitors sit five points above the drop zone thanks to a win and a draw in their last two outings.

Sheffield United head back into Championship action after the international break on Saturday aiming to reignite their pursuit of the playoff places.

Aiming to kick on from a 13th-placed finish in 2025-26 and challenge for a return to the Premier League, the Blades experienced a mixed start to the season but looked to have turned a corner after the September and October break.

The Blades managed four wins and one draw in their first six games back from that break, scoring 11 goals and conceding six in those games, culminating in a 1-0 home victory over Wrexham, with Ben Brereton Diaz on the scoresheet, and a 3-2 away victory against Preston North End thanks to Sydie Peck's hat-trick.

They were unable to carry that winning streak into the latest break, though, visiting Charlton Athletic last time out and losing 2-1, having fallen behind and levelled through Jordan Ayew before Matt Godden scored the winner for their hosts 10 minutes from time.

Now sat 10th but just two points behind seventh and eighth spots, Sheffield United will again hope to come back firing and return to winning ways at Bramall Lane on Saturday.

Their visitors, meanwhile, head to South Yorkshire aiming to build on a positive turn in form before the break.

After a 16th-placed Championship finish in 2025-26 and the summer appointment of Alessio Dionisi, Watford endured a poor start to the fresh campaign, picking up just 11 points from their first 13 matches, winning three and losing eight of those.

The Hornets' away record is a real cause for concern, having lost six and drawn one of their seven league matches on the road, scoring just four goals in those and conceding 14.

The most recent of those was a 3-2 away loss against Norwich City, in which they led 2-0 at the break, but Dionisi's men did bounce back, beating Lincoln City 1-0 at home thanks to Stephy Mavididi's goal, before they hosted then-leaders Middlesbrough last time out and stood strong for a point from a 0-0 draw.

Watford now return to action hoping to add to those positive results and extend their five-point lead over the relegation zone.

Sheffield United Championship form:.

Sheffield Wednesday are unable to call on defender Femi Seriki, who sustained a long-term injury before the break, while Matt Doherty, Ryan One and Joe Rothwell may also remain sidelined.

Patrick Bamford may be in line for a return, though, having been out with a shoulder injury, and if deemed fit he could return up front from the start despite competition for those places from Ben Brereton Diaz, Tom Cannon, Jordan Ayew and Tyrese Campbell.

Kalvin Phillips has impressed in his second loan spell with the Blades thus far and will again join Sydie Peck in midfield.

Watford are still without Kwadwo Baah, Jeremy Ngakia, Soumaila Coulibaly and Edoardo Bove on Saturday due to ongoing injuries.

Kevin Keben and Branimir Mlacic should again join Mattie Pollock in the middle of the defence after their clean sheet against Middlesbrough last time out, while Krepin Diatta may start in a wing-back role if he is fit after being forced off in that game.

Competition for attacking spots is rife with Mamadou Doumbia, Amin Nabizada, Stephy Mavididi, Luca Kjerrumgaard, Rocco Vata and Othmane Maamma all pushing to start, while Myron Boadu has often led the line but missed the Middlesbrough game.

Sheffield United possible starting lineup:.

Cooper; Choudhury, Tanganga, Kitching, Burrows; Donovan, Peck, Phillips, Brereton Diaz; Cannon, Bamford.

Watford possible starting lineup:.

Ravaglia; Diatta, Keben, Pollock, Mlacic, Zemura; Kayembe, Kyprianou, Bravo; Mavididi, Doumbia.

Watford highlighted signs of improvement before the break with consecutive clean sheets, but we fancy Sheffield United, rested after a disappointing defeat halted their notable improvement, to bounce back at Bramall Lane.

Jashari has once again found himself playing largely as a back-up under Ruben Amorim this season, after performing the role of being Luka Modric’s deputy during his debut campaign with the Rossoneri under Massimiliano Allegri.

It has been revealed that given that over €30m was invested to sign him from Club Brugge, a bigger role and impact was perhaps foreseen by all parties. Thus, Jashari’s situation is one to monitor, and there is certainly no shortage of interested parties.

According to information from 4-4-2.ch, clubs in both Serie A and the Premier League are seriously considering a move for the 24-year-old midfielder, who started last night in Switzerland’s 4-0 win over Scotland and impressed.

A permanent sale would therefore require a fee in the range of €35-40m. Milan paid Club Brugge a similar sum for him a year ago and they have no intention of making a loss, given his age and potential.

The old rivals did battle in the Carabao Cup in September and Chelsea emerged as 6-3 victors at Stamford Bridge.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Xabi Alonso’s men are due to host Leeds again tomorrow (November 21) and Justin has made it clear a stern test lies ahead.

He told Premier League Studios, as quoted by the official Leeds website: “I feel like it will be a bit of a different side than what we faced in the League Cup tie, and we know they are a team that likes to play in the small spaces.

“They have got talent spilling out and you have to keep control of that but also try and take advantage of somewhere they might not be as tight, obviously.

“They lost their last match against Sunderland so hopefully we can look at that match and learn a few things.”.

Leeds returned to winning ways prior to the international break, defeating Chelsea’s London rivals Tottenham Hotspur 1-0.

Daniel Farke’s men may well be the underdogs but just two points separate the fifth-placed Blues and ninth-placed Whites.

Industry observers note that justin said: “It has been nice to rest and recharge a little bit, and work on a few things on the training pitch. We are ready to go and pick things up again.

Industry observers note that “I would say from last season we have come on leaps and bounds and the confidence that everyone has in the squad is a lot more compared to this time last season. We have still got a way to go but we have had a solid start.”.

Leeds indicated ambition with their summer transfer window recruitment, splashing out a club-record £40m on England international goalkeeper James Trafford.

They also bolstered in the centre of defence by recruiting Tarik Muharemović and Nico Elvedi, who have been partnering Justin in a back three.

Sources indicate that justin remarked: “We obviously added some quality players in the summer. We are looking at this season and first and foremost to cement our place in the Premier League. Who knows what can happen after that.

Sources indicate that “We had a few rocky results before [Spurs] and maybe didn’t quite get the results that we were looking for or deserved, which happens in football. Sometimes you are going to win games you don’t deserve and vice versa.

According to recent reports, “The Premier League is difficult. The game changes in tiny moments and teams are so closely matched that all it takes is one lapse of concentration or one moment of magic to break the deadlock. Then, you are chasing the game and every team can defend well in the Premier League.

Recent findings suggest that “We are more on the front foot in most of the games and looking for ways to decide the game and taking the initiative. That is something that we would like to continue this season and it will be no different traveling to London this weekend.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Ben Sully | 19 Nov 2026 23:48, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 01:22.
  • AFC Wimbledon will be looking to claim a second straight win when they make the short trip to Brisbane Road for Saturday's League One clash against Leyton Orient.
  • The O's, meanwhile, are bidding to record a fourth consecutive home victory in all competitions.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Ben Sully | 19 Nov 2026 23:48, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 01:22.

AFC Wimbledon will be looking to claim a second straight win when they make the short trip to Brisbane Road for Saturday's League One clash against Leyton Orient.

The O's, meanwhile, are bidding to record a fourth consecutive home victory in all competitions.

Leyton Orient head into the weekend in 14th spot in the League One table after recording five wins, two draws and six defeats in their 13 league games this term.

Orient cruised to a 3-0 victory in their most recent league outing against Cambridge United at the end of October, a result that has formed part of a three-game winning run on home turf.

Their last victory at Brisbane Road took place in the FA Cup first round, which saw Idris El Mizouni net a brace in an emphatic 5-1 win over sixth-tier Harborough Town to set up a second-round tie against Port Vale.

However, Richie Wellens's side were unable to repeat that sort of success in their away clash against Barnet in the EFL Trophy, falling to a 4-2 defeat as they finished at the bottom of Group F and behind third-place Wimbledon on goal difference.

Orient will now return to the familiar surroundings of Brisbane Road, where they have won four of their last five outings, including three victories without conceding in their previous four home league games.

That represents a significant improvement from the start of the season when they lost each of their opening three home matches in the third tier.

Wimbledon have played a game more than Orient, but they are a point worse off after winning four, drawing four and losing six of their 14 League One matches.

In fact, the Dons have lost four of their previous six games in the third tier, although they did manage to end an 11-game winless run in all competitions in their most recent outing against Blackpool.

Alistair Smith's first-half proved enough to fire Wimbledon to a 1-0 victory, representing their first three-point haul since recording back-to-back wins against Bromley and Doncaster Rovers in September.

After enjoying success at Plough Lane, Johnnie Jackson's side will now make the trip to Brisbane Road for the second time this season after playing out a 1-1 draw in August's EFL Trophy encounter.

They missed out on a bonus point with a defeat in the subsequent penalty shootout, but they enjoyed greater success in January's league visit, when they fought back from a goal down to claim a 3-1 victory.

However, their hopes of repeating that success may be tempered by the fact they have lost six of their last eight competitive away games, including each of their last four.

AFC Wimbledon form (all competitions):.

Orient midfielder Ollie O’Neill will be out for around four months after undergoing an operation not long after returning from a long injury absence.

The hosts are also expected to be without the services of Nicholas Oyekunle, Demetri Mitchell and Sean Clare.

Rarmani Edmonds-Green will feature alongside Alfie Gilchrist in central defence after returning from injury to start the wins over Cambridge and Harborough.

As for the visitors, Wimbledon are unable to call upon Josef Bursik, Dan Sweeney, Dujuan Richards, Ryan Johnson and Donnell McNeilly due to injury.

Jayden Stockley will serve a one-match ban after being sent off for two bookable offences in the narrow win over Blackpool.

Aaron Sasu could move forward to replace Stockley in the frontline, which would open the door for Steven Sessegnon to feature at left wing-back.

Sam Winnall has conceded he “probably didn’t realise” how intense the rivalry between Barnsley and Sheffield Wednesday was when he swapped the Reds for the Owls in 2017.

The now retired 35-year-old was a talismanic figure in his Barnsley days, scoring 48 goals across 155 appearances for the club.

He was lured away from Oakwell in January 2017, making a controversial move to their South Yorkshire neighbours Wednesday.

The move sparked anger among Barnsley supporters and Winnall received a frosty reception when he faced the Reds as a Wednesday player.

Industry observers note that “A lot of what happened was actually well out of my control,” he told The Star. “And I think you look back with not so much regrets from what I can control, but more so just wishing it could have happened at a different time, if I'm going to be totally honest.

According to recent reports, “And I look back on it with fond memories, actually, because I think it was a transfer that brought me a few difficulties but I came through it and came out the other side. I grew a level of resilience with what had happened. I don't look back on it with any regrets of how I acted personally.

It has been revealed that “People do move between rival clubs. Mine was obviously at a lower level but look at Sol Campbell, Carlos Tevez, it’s football. But I do definitely look back and think it could have been done more professionally.”.

Winnall added fuel to the fire when he returned to Oakwell just months after departing, scoring in a 1-1 draw and celebrating in front of the home supporters.

In a recent development, “It's probably been my most asked question since I've retired,” he said. “And do you know what? I look back and if I could have the chance again, I'd do exactly the same.

It has been revealed that “That's because it had been quite a difficult time. I'd had quite a lot of stick from different fans and even some former teammates that had spoken about me in the press. I felt a little bit let down by that. I will say this, it was never meant to kind of upset or create any kind of animosity towards any of the Barnsley fans at all.”.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • 'It was like meeting a kid at a sixth-form careers day'.
  • When, at England's World Cup base in Kansas City, I then sat down with Trafford and he revealed that his partner had packed some Lego for him to build in camp, you wondered if sixth-form was a grade too high.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By CRAIG HOPE, CHIEF FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 14:00 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 16:35 EST, 16 November 2026.

'It was like meeting a kid at a sixth-form careers day'. That was the verdict, slightly unflattering but endearing all the same, of one Premier League chief after encountering James Trafford.

When, at England's World Cup base in Kansas City, I then sat down with Trafford and he revealed that his partner had packed some Lego for him to build in camp, you wondered if sixth-form was a grade too high.

He is the son of a Cumbrian farmer and the Lego was of a tractor, which he would save for later in the tournament. 'You don't want to go too early,' he said.

None of this is a criticism. Far from it. There was a boyish charm, an innocence, even, and Trafford was engaging tech giant. Nonetheless, he did not sound ready for the likes of a World Cup semi-final against Argentina. Thomas Tuchel agreed.

But every boy will one day become a man. On a ferocious and febrile night in Madrid, no place for adolescents, we may just have witnessed James Trafford's graduation ceremony.

Industry observers note that without his double save in stoppage-time, England would have left Spain without a famous, and deserved, victory. One Spanish title labelled it 'la actuacion de su vida', the performance of his life. You wonder how much they saw of his loan spell at Accrington Stanley, but the sentiment stands.

James Trafford celebrates with Jarell Quansah, Dan Burn and Ezri Konsa during his starring performance in Spain.

Trafford pictured with his farmer father, David, in the cab of his tractor with their dogs (Source: James Trafford).

Industry observers note that madrid daily AS exclaimed: 'Magisterio de Trafford!' Translated, 'A Trafford Masterclass!'. They claim he was the reason Spain could not complete their comeback, and they would be right.

When Tuchel stood with us in a corridor of the Metropolitano Stadium on the eve of the game, he had no glitch confirming that Trafford would start. His message, though, was clear - it was sink or swim for a goalkeeper who turned 24 last month.

Sources indicate that not only did Trafford keep his head above water, it was he who pulled the team ashore. It was he to whom his senior colleagues ran in celebration. Ezri Konsa nearly took the shirt off Trafford's back, such was the force of his gratitude. But maybe this was the occasion when Trafford took the No 1 jersey from the back of Jordan Pickford, the holder for nearly a decade.

It has been revealed that pickford has done nothing wrong. Were Trafford to still display that maturity deficit, Pickford would be a reliable custodian heading to Euro 2028. This is not Peter Shilton post Italia 90, an uncomfortable truth of a great in need of the retirement barn. The 32-year-old has plenty to give on the back of all he has already given.

This, admitted Tuchel after the 3-2 win, is a selection dilemma that allows a manager to sleep well at night.

Recent findings suggest that 'There is no headache at all!' he boomed. 'I'm so far away from a headache, I cannot imagine.

Trafford left Manchester City with the initiative to usurp Jordan Pickford as England No 1.

Jude Bellingham certainly seemed impressed with the performance of the goalkeeper.

Recent findings suggest that 'This is what we wanted. This is the best thing that can happen to all of us, also to Pickers. It is amazing how they push each other, and if then Traff has a performance like this, he has it because he knows he's well prepared. He gets the push from his colleagues and competitors.'.

Recent findings suggest that tuchel has seen enough of Trafford in training and around camp to believe he is ready for promotion. He has watched him for Leeds, where he rates as the best performing goalkeeper in the Premier League. His 'net goals prevented' (4.4) and 'save percentage' (81.4) are higher than any rival this season, including Pickford.

'You always have to deserve your place,' added Tuchel. 'You will never get a gift and just get a game (for the sake of it). So he deserved to play and we expected this kind of performance. It was not only the last save, but also the build-up play and not losing focus. He has proved it on this stage, so this gives him a lot of belief. Now, it's on him to keep going for it.'.

Sources indicate that it, you presume, is the No 1 jersey. Trafford has made no secret of his desire to take it from Pickford, and he told us in the summer that such ambition was the motivation behind him wanting to leave Manchester City for a second time.

That day, he flipped his room key with a magician's sleight of hand throughout the interview, a dexterity useful for Lego. Better still for fingertip saves such as the one to deny Aymeric Laporte in the 91st minute.

Recent findings suggest that also in the gift pack from his girlfriend were two face masks. 'Very thoughtful,' he quipped. But that is another observation, bordering on concern, that some prospective buyers have made in recent years - on the goalkeeping scale of uber professional to joker, he resides too close to the latter. We have seen, even this season, the odd concentration lapse that speaks to that thought.

Trafford has played a starring role in goal since moving to Leeds United in the summer.

But there was also a feeling that Trafford needed more exposure and responsibility before the penny dropped and his value was realised. Already, £95million has been spent on him in transfer fees.

At Leeds, and now with England, he has been given that stage, as Tuchel calls it. The head coach maintains that Pickford is his first choice, but it was Trafford he picked for both Nations League fixtures against Spain, the ones that really mattered, the ones that would strengthen or threaten his own employment.

As for Trafford's career prospects, to revisit our opening line, England's No 1 sounds like a fair vocation.

Thomas Tuchel wants England to use victory in the Nations League finals as a springboard to winning Euro 2028 at Wembley.

The head coach admits it has taken him a while to recover from the trauma of his side’s World Cup semi-final defeat by Argentina in July, for which he was heavily criticised.

But after beating world champions Spain 3-2 on Sunday night, topping their Nations League group ahead of March’s quarter-finals and next summer's finals, Tuchel is finally able to look forward with positivity and belief.

‘I saw the celebrations in Portugal when they won the Nations League,’ he remarked. ‘It’s just the best, the best preparation we can have for the Euros. We want to have these matches on the highest level to prove ourselves and to gain confidence, to see where we are and to adjust our game where we need to, that’s what this Nations League is perfect for. We want to win it.’.

England have won five of their six matches since the World Cup, losing only to Spain at Wembley in September. In the build up to that game, Tuchel was involved in heated exchanges with observers who continued to question his tactics in the final half hour against Argentina.

’It took me a while to digest (the World Cup exit) and see the way forward, how we can help and adjust and improve, and how we can do this together,’ he stated.

It has been revealed that ‘We had reviews and so on, but clarity then came together with the players. Straight away we had the energy right to take the next steps. The ideas became more clear for me, even if it was not so easy the first week, to overcome and arrive with different emotions. Some were still upset from the World Cup. Some were latest in the team. Some had digested it, some had not digested it. But it was key to have this kind of process together.

In a recent development, ‘(Spain) was a complete performance that makes me very proud. It's a full package of belief, of courage, of commitment, of togetherness, of relying on each other and stepping up in this moment.’.

Tuchel, though, has rejected the idea that seeing out the win Madrid was proof that he has learned from his mistakes in Atlanta.

‘Not at all, I think we would not have been in this situation if it was 11 against 11,’ he remarked. ‘For me, it was Mexico reloaded (not Argentina). It's one man down, but what can you do? It is their strength to have ball possession, to overload and find the gaps. It just plays totally into their hands and it comes wave after wave. It felt like three hours and thirty minutes!’.

  • On their return to league action after a weekend off for the international break, Luton Town will head to the Pirelli Stadium to take on Burton Albion on Saturday.
  • The visitors sit five points outside of the top two in the League One table in the midst of a seven-game unbeaten streak in all competitions while their hosts are 15th after consecutive league defeats.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Sam Varley | 19 Nov 2026 23:48.

On their return to league action after a weekend off for the international break, Luton Town will head to the Pirelli Stadium to take on Burton Albion on Saturday.

The visitors sit five points outside of the top two in the League One table in the midst of a seven-game unbeaten streak in all competitions while their hosts are 15th after consecutive league defeats.

Burton Albion head into the weekend aiming to bounce back from a pair of defeats and move back towards the top half of League One.

Aiming to build on a 17th-placed finish last time around, the Brewers enjoyed a positive start to the new term, earning 17 points from their first 13 outings courtesy of four wins, five draws and four defeats.

That was largely thanks to a solid home record, having only lost once in seven league outings at the Pirelli Stadium, most recently beating Leyton Orient 2-1, only to suffer consecutive away losses in their last two third-tier games.

A trip to Wycombe Wanderers ended in a 2-0 loss, before they followed up consecutive cup matches with a visit to MK Dons and suffered a 6-2 beating, having fallen 3-0 and 6-1 behind with goals from Emeka Adiele and Kain Adom nothing more than consolations.

Now sat 15th, but just two points off 11th-placed Leicester City, Burton Albion will bid to put those league defeats behind them and bounce back to winning ways at the Pirelli Stadium.

They face another tough test, though, as the visitors arrive aiming to continue an unbeaten run and narrow their gap to the league leaders.

In their first full season under Jack Wilshere, after falling agonisingly short in their playoff pursuit under him late last season, Luton Town right now sit fourth with 24 points on the board from 14 games.

The Hatters lost four of their first nine league games but have since bounced back in style, rebounding from the last of those with four straight wins over Barnsley, Leicester City, Doncaster Rovers and Peterborough United.

A trip to league leaders Huddersfield Town then followed, and Wilshere's men left with a creditable point from a 1-1 draw having led through Jordan Clark and been pegged back by Joe Taylor, before they hosted Forest Green Rovers in the FA Cup first round before the international break and won 2-0 with Emilio Lawrence and Clark on the scoresheet.

Now on the back of a free weekend last time out due to international call-ups, and a 3-0 EFL Trophy win over Peterborough United on Tuesday as Clark again scored alongside Nahki Wells and Devante Cole, Luton Town turn their focus back to League One and will hope to narrow their five-point gap to the top two with a fifth win in six league matches on Saturday.

Burton Albion form (all competitions):.

Luton Town form (all competitions):.

Burton Albion are set to remain without Finn Delap, George Evans, Kyran Lofthouse and Caylan Vickers on Saturday due to injuries.

Matthew Dennis also missed their last game, and in his and Vickers's expected absence, Mark O'Mahony should again lead the line for the Brewers.

He should again have support from star man Charlie Webster and Kain Adom who scored against MK Dons last time out, while Kegs Chauke is a mainstay in midifeld.

Luton Town are still unable to call on the injured trio of Hakeem Odoffin, Gideon Kodua and Shayden Morris, who is yet to feature this season.

Wilshere fielded a strong starting XI for their midweek EFL Trophy tie with Peterborough and the Hatters will look similar on Saturday, with Wells continuing to lead the line having netted his ninth goal of the season in that win.

He will have support from Kasey Palmer and Jordan Clark, who also scored last time out to make it a goal in each of his last four games, while Dan Gore will hope to continue alongside midfield mainstay Liam Walsh despite Wilshere often fielding another attacking midfielder in League One action.

Burton Albion possible starting lineup:.

Addai; Araujo, Tilt, Sibbick; Borges Rodrigues, Chauke, Krubally, Adiele; Webster, O'Mahony, Adom.

Luton Town possible starting lineup:.

Shea; Jones, Andersen, Johnston, Ashby; Walsh; Richards, Clark, Donley, Palmer; Wells.

Burton Albion have seen their resilient start to the season halted in recent weeks, and we see them falling short against a strong Luton team who have won six of their last seven matches in all competitions.

More than just a football club: Cardinale’s vision to make AC Milan a multi-billion empire

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In case you weren’t aware from his repeatedly bold comments in the media, Gerry Cardinale has massive plans for AC Milan.
  • Industry observers note that the RedBird Capital founder and chief has made one concept very clear: while he is at the helm, Milan are no longer just a football club, but a platform that aims to integrate sports, infrastructure, and entertainment.
  • Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In case you weren’t aware from his repeatedly bold comments in the media, Gerry Cardinale has massive plans for AC Milan.

Industry observers note that the RedBird Capital founder and chief has made one concept very clear: while he is at the helm, Milan are no longer just a football club, but a platform that aims to integrate sports, infrastructure, and entertainment. Of course AC Milan will be at the centre of the web, but the idea is to expand.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Recent findings suggest that the proof of this comes from a three-letter acronym: MSE. It stands for Milan Sports & Entertainment and it is the new holding company created by RedBird. The idea, simply put, is to bring together investments and activities in various sectors under one umbrella.

As La Gazzetta dello Sport recall, Cardinale explained to the Financial Times that the assets involved could be valued in the mid-single-digit billions, meaning several billion dollars. So, how does he plan to get there?

Cardinale linked the creation of MSE to the process initiated with the acquisition of Milan: “Milan Sports & Entertainment is the culmination of this work and of what we have built since we first invested in the club four years ago.”.

In his interview with La Gazzetta, Cardinale clarified that the newly introduced structure is also created to support the Rossoneri’s sporting ambitions: “The driving force behind operations like this is to provide Milan with the financial strength needed to compete in the transfer market and secure the best players in the world.”.

There are examples of this kind of model working already. Kroenke Sports & Entertainment, AEG and Fenway Sports Group are among the most prominent and – given his background in the USA – Cardinale knows each of them well.

According to CNBC valuations, KSE was worth $26.05bn in 2026, FSG $15.37bn, and AEG $11.99bn in 2025, excluding music and hotel businesses.

KSE boasts franchises such as the Los Angeles Rams, Denver Nuggets, Colorado Avalanche and Arsenal, as well as venues such as SoFi Stadium, Ball Arena, and Emirates Stadium. The group combines sports, infrastructure and real estate development such as Hollywood Park, the district built around SoFi Stadium.

Recent findings suggest that AEG – founded by Philip Anschutz – have instead built its model on the management and development of venues. It owns or manages venues such as Crypto.com Arena and The O2 in London plus the Los Angeles Kings and LA Galaxy, and operates in concert promotion and ticketing. The LA LIVE project developed around Crypto.com Arena puts the venue at the centre of a greater ecosystem.

Fenway Sports Group – born around the Boston Red Sox and Liverpool FC – have developed a holding company with interests in media, marketing, real estate, and entertainment. It’s a model Cardinale knows first hand: in 2021, RedBird invested approximately $750m in FSG, acquiring a stake of around 11%, based on an enterprise valuation of $7.35bn.

Recent findings suggest that MSE in theory can harness elements of all three of these experiences: KSE’s integration of sports and infrastructure, AEG ‘s commercial development of facilities and FSG ‘s multi-sport approach. The main difference is the purpose declared by Cardinale: to use all of it to funnel money back into Milan.

From the stadium shared with Inter to the possibility of an arena in San Donato, including the new NBA Europe venture and even tennis: MSE’s scope includes various initiatives that go beyond the playing field.

The main infrastructure project is the future Generali Stadium, the fresh 71,500-seat facility designed by Foster + Partners and Manica. Developed jointly by the two Milanese clubs, it represents a key element of the transformation of the San Siro area and will not be a Rossoneri-only facility.

Sources indicate that the promoters intend for the stadium to host year-round activities, from matches to concerts, as well as catering, events, and hospitality services. In other words, like the stadiums and arenas mentioned above, it will become more than just a place to go for two hours on a Sunday.

According to recent reports, in San Donato Milanese, RedBird are also considering the possibility of building a 20,000-seat arena. Cardinale explained that the fund already owns the land and has planning permission, but the idea is also linked to Milan’s potential involvement in NBA Europe. Another area of ​​focus concerns tennis, with the possibility of hosting a tournament in the city.

Finally, RedBird intend to develop a company dedicated to managing stadiums and arenas, with services including catering, merchandising and premium hospitality. The goal is to build commercial expertise to apply to the facilities connected to the group, but also to make it available to other owners and sports clubs.

It has been revealed that this phase will be co-ordinated by Brett Yormark, appointed CEO of MSE and set to step down as head of the Major 12 (a conference in College Football) at the end of January 2027. He worked for 14 years at Brooklyn Sports & Entertainment, overseeing the development of the Brooklyn Nets and the Barclays Center. He has also gained experience in NASCAR and Roc Nation.

The choice to go for Yormark reflects the desire to entrust the platform to someone with expertise across multiple different fields in the sporting and commercial worlds.

It has been revealed that all these grand intends are well and good, but how will ideas turn into money that drives AC Milan forward? MSE’s economic potential is measured not only through the club’s revenues, but also through the activities that RedBird intends to develop around sports, infrastructure and entertainment.

It has been revealed that the starting point is obviously Milan as a club, which closed the 2025-26 financial year with revenues of €464.6m, over €100m of which came from sponsorships. The main infrastructure opportunity is the new San Siro, an investment of approximately €2.3bn shared with Inter.

Projections contained in the design documents indicate a potential annual revenue of approximately €120.4m for the facility as a whole (both for the Rossoneri and the Nerazzurri), through sporting, commercial, and complementary services.

According to recent reports, these are numbers that will be revised upwards by the two clubs when considering, for example, the record agreement with Generali for naming rights. It is worth a total of €650m over 25 years, divided into €10m per year for the first five years and €30m per season for the following 20, once the stadium is built.

According to recent reports, one of the areas on which RedBird Capital are focusing most is hospitality, which is currently worth around €15m per year for the Rossoneri. The international benchmark has already been set by Legends Global, a manufacturer Cardinale knows well.

According to recent reports, legends are what the Milan owner sees as a model for developing premium services, restaurants, and commercial spaces. The most obvious example is at FC Barcelona: with the support of LG, the club have marketed nearly 5,000 VIP seats at Camp Nou, generating over €380m in contracted revenue.

They aim to generate another €700m through multi-year licenses for an additional 2,000 seats. This isn’t annual revenue, but rather contracts spread over 15 or 30 years, so a guaranteed flow of money coming in that Cardinale aims to replicate.

Another agreement which demonstrates the potential of this kind of arrangement is the one with Real Madrid for the Santiago Bernabéu. It involves an investment of approximately €360m in exchange for 20-year participation in some of the stadium’s businesses,.

According to recent reports, legends Global also operate in facilities and events management. Following the acquisition of ASM Global (who actually proposed renovating San Siro for non-football events in Italy) in 2024, the group claims a presence in over 450 venues, approximately 20,000 events, and 165 million guests annually. Their European partnerships include Arsenal, Chelsea and Porto.

FC Barcelona releases upcoming VIP seating licenses at Spotify Camp Nou with Legends Global.

🔗 More details: https://t.co/awtEsnYE6X pic.twitter.com/iCMuM0QD35.

— FC Barcelona (@FCBarcelona) September 25, 2026.

To illustrate the potential it could hold for Italy as a whole, the English subsidiary reported revenues of £131.6m in 2024, of which £105.5m came from facility and event management and £26.1m from catering. Before the integration with ASM Global, Legends had reported revenues of $1.7bn in the period ending in March 2024, with 67% coming from food and beverage sales.

According to recent reports, in Italy, a benchmark is Forumnet, who in 2024 generated €29.7m in revenue and €12.8m in EBITDA (Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation). They manage the Assago Forum which hosts approximately 60-70 concerts a year, demonstrating how a venue can generate activity well beyond the sports calendar.

Sources indicate that as mentioned, an arena is being planned in San Donato with an estimated investment of around €400m, which could become the basis for a Milanese franchise in NBA Europe. For reference, Olimpia Milano – the current basketball team in the city – generate around €15m through ticketing, season tickets, sponsorships and merchandising.

For NBA Europe, projections speak of over $1.5bn to be distributed to the clubs in the first six years. A theoretical division among the 12 permanent franchises would equate to approximately $20.8m per team per year, but this is not fixed yet. Entry costs – estimated by the media to be between $500m and over $1bn – also remain to be determined.

Tennis represents another potential area for development. The ATP 500 in Halle generates around €5m in revenue, excluding television rights, while the ATP Finals in Turin generate around €60m. These are events with different dimensions and scopes, but they provide a scale.

The creation of MSE has a stated objective: to strengthen Milan’s financial capacity and reduce the gap with the richest clubs on the international scene, particularly those in the Premier League.

Sources indicate that the gap is also evident when comparing revenues. AC Milan closed the 2025-26 season with €464.6m, a significant result considering their absence from European competitions , but still far from the top English clubs.

In a recent development, according to the Deloitte Football Money League, in the 2024-25 season, Liverpool generated €836.1m, Arsenal €821.7m and Manchester United €793.1m. Tottenham and Chelsea also exceeded €670m and €580m, respectively.

Industry observers note that the comparison covers different financial years, but it still demonstrates the magnitude of the gap. Liverpool generated revenues equal to approximately 1.8 times those of Milan, while Chelsea recorded a turnover approximately €120 higher.

The chasm highlights how clubs in the Premier League have showcased an ability to generate commercial revenue, enhance stadiums and reach a global audience. The gap has only been growing, and TV rights will be another focus, though that is outside of just Cardinale’s hands.

Industry observers note that speaking of the owner, it is now obvious he sees MSE as the name that will house the tools to try build a real sporting and commercial world around Milan. It remains to be seen how effective it will be, but the starting point is there.

He has not yet made a first-team appearance, but he has been on Farke’s bench and is already being named in senior Wales squads.

According to the Daily Mail’s Tom Collomosse, the defender has caught the eye of several Championship clubs who could explore a loan deal in January.

Posting on X, he mentioned: “Leeds very excited about Jayden Lienou, 18-year-old left-back in full Wales squad. Lienou has been training with first team since February and featured in summer.

Lienou is well thought of in LS11 but regular first-team action may prove hard to come by if he stays put. Not only does Farke have Sweden international Gabriel Gudmundsson in his left-back department, the Leeds boss can call upon former France youth international Melvin Bard.

Lienou penned a new contract at Elland Road in the summer and after committing to the Whites until 2029, he said: “It feels amazing - another step in the right direction, and another step towards where me and my family want me to get to in the future.

“I'd say I'm probably further ahead than I thought I was going to be when I first signed for Leeds. When me and Scott sat down at the start of the season we set some goals to get to certain situations, certain milestones in my career and I think I've exceeded that.

“Getting the support from all the different people, the different knowledge, the different views on different points that they can give across just helps you develop as a player, especially coming through as a young player at the club.”.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Industry observers note that admittedly, the task was made significantly easier by the major turning point of this game: a red card for Brentford’s Yehor Yarmoliuk.
